design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (appraisal_orders_and_fees)

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[4, 6]. The late-rush refund takes 4 factors, the final inspection charge 6.

[Why a good test] Owen Hadley only asks to pay for the appraiser's return visit for the completion sign-off. The figure (90.00) is fixed only after the order's fee history shows the refund owed on a rush charge whose promise was missed ('The final inspection charge is fixed only after the order's fee history shows the refund owed on any rush charge whose promised delivery date was missed.'). The agent must see that he paid rush after intent to proceed, that the report arrived after the 2026-09-11 due date and that no refund stands; work the refund (120.00) from four rules (counting endpoint set by the value-changing reconsideration, lateness share, closing slip, borrower-borne lock extension cost) over the order, its ledger, the loan file and the lock's pricing history; book it to the rush card; and only then price the visit from six inputs (netted re-visit base, scheduled closing date, FHA program, standing outlay, partner-builder credit, late-original share) and hand the payment to the borrower.

[Scope] Occupied by task 0: appraisal_ext_size_value_addon + appraisal_ext_update_inspection_charge with book_size_value_addon_5d867e2e and pay_update_inspection_charge_fc307ba0. Claimed here: appraisal_ext_late_rush_refund (agent, refund_late_rush_charge_6e5bda3a, state_due) and appraisal_ext_final_inspection_charge (user, pay_final_inspection_charge_e30bacb7, on_request). Disjoint tools, policies and triggering facts: this report is inside its validity days at the scheduled closing, so the completion charge (not the update visit charge) governs the visit. Together the two tasks cover all four extended policies.

[Problem-tree card] root = appraisal_ext_final_inspection_charge (owner=user). Edge -> appraisal_ext_late_rush_refund: value_input, gate binding rush_miss_refunds, form state, sentence in the affirmative direction ('fixed only after'), the way a fee desk states that a charge rests on what precedes it (task 0's sentence uses the negated 'not fixed until', so the charter carries both directions). Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; waited-on side is a record-visible state (a refund entry for a missed rush promise on the fee history); no tool/id/code token; scope 'any rush charge whose promised delivery date was missed' matches the policy's open set. Exactly one write of the difficulty books a refund with that reason: the late-rush refund policy's target tool. Derivation: sentence + fee history (rush 150.00, no refund) + order dates (due 09-11, completed 09-12, delivered 09-15) and the value-changing decision of 09-16 + the refund policy rule -> book the late-rush refund. Unresolved at frozen_time: ledger eebc1eec rush_fee with no refund; fee_balance 1220.00. Order: refund (action 11) then payment (action 13). Deletion run: skipping the refund -> charge 120.00 instead of 90.00. Persona never mentions rush, lateness or refunds; tools block nothing.

[Factor card — late-rush refund, expected 120.00, whole baseline 150.00]
- lateness_share_tier (parameter): 5 days late -> 50 percent; baseline 100 -> 150.00.
- days_late_endpoint (method, anchor of the late count): the factual-error reconsideration 87d5fe64 changed the value on 2026-09-16 -> count to that decided date (5 days); baseline counts to the completed date (1 day -> 25 percent) -> 82.50. Near-miss: the completed date (1 day); the delivered date (4 days) is the unreached second tier.
- closing_slip_points (parameter, cross-difficulty loan): scheduled closing 2026-10-22 is 13 days after the contract closing 2026-10-09 -> +20; baseline 0 -> 90.00.
- extension_cost_points (parameter, cross-difficulty lock XSUM of lock_pricing_events on the file's lock): extension dce7a1bc, 622.12 borne by the borrower, no waiver -> +10; baseline 0 -> 105.00.
Scope exclusions (not factors): cancelled orders, HPML flip second appraisals and rush charges collected before intent to proceed are refunded in full by the base fee refund policy and stay outside this rule; this order is inside it.
Overwrite declared: base 'rush_fee is refunded in full (rush_deadline_missed)' sentence replaced by the share rule. The refund's days late are its own count; the base turn_time 'appraisal delay' definition is not retired and stays in force for the add-on arrival rule, the final inspection charge's late-original share and the lock charter.
[Factor card — final inspection charge, expected 90.00, whole baseline 200.00]
- revisit_base_method (method: netted re-visit — reinspection fee less recent reinspection charges, floored at the trip fee / fresh visit plus travel / reinspection fee): reinspection charge 120.00 on 2026-09-28 -> max(125, 200-120) = 125.00; baseline 200.00 -> 146.25.
- signing_turn_tier (parameter, cross funding): scheduled closing date 2026-10-22, 8 days -> 75.00; baseline -> 33.75.
- government_program_tier (parameter, cross loan): FHA -> 50.00; baseline -> 52.50.
- standing_outlay_tier (parameter, history over every charge and refund): 1,100.00 -> 30.00 off; baseline -> 112.50.
- partner_builder_tier (parameter, cross credit): Builder Partner Credit verified -> 100.00 off; baseline -> 165.00.
- late_original_share (parameter, multi-source: refund for missed rush AND completed-vs-due days, value_input): 1 day -> 75 percent; baseline 100 -> 120.00. Near-miss: the delivered date (4 days after due) or the refund's 5-day count would give 50 percent; this share reads completed-versus-due days.
Task floors: multi-source = late_original_share; cross-difficulty = closing_slip_points (loan), extension_cost_points (lock), signing_turn_tier (funding), government_program_tier (loan), partner_builder_tier (credit).

[Base-invariant card] Refund write, subject appraisal_fee_refunded: governing appraisal_fee_refund, gate charge_not_refunded (dedup): the rush entry eebc1eec has no refund naming it; the call passes it as original_fee_entry_id. Charge write, subject appraisal_fee_charged: appraisal_fee_schedule.after_itp_only (loan file status clear_to_close is allowed; loan_file_id passed), appraisal_validity_and_update and appraisal_hpml_flip_second_appraisal as policy_scope (report 44 days old at closing, inside 180; not HPML). No time gates on these writes. Final inspection charge overwrites: validity completion clause (replacement keeps 'before funding' and names the update visit charge's combined visit and the new-order case), fee_schedule reinspection sentence and 'no stacking or discount' sentence (each scoped to its own parts and naming the siblings'); the base rush charge at order stays in force (the closing-turn part is a turn-time premium, not a rush charge).

[Business-object card] Target: appraisal order b55276e3 on loan file 1beb0ad2. Refund correlates to the rush entry eebc1eec only (base, trip and reinspection entries excluded by fee_component). The final inspection charge is the return visit after the 2026-09-28 completion visit (entry 2ae8d65f), which the re-visit rule nets. Cross rows: lock 9a840dde + its extension dce7a1bc (cost 622.12 = 9 charged days x 2 bps x 345,624.40, 6 borne days = 5 complimentary + 1 appraisal-delay day), closing d9f58bff scheduled, Builder Partner Credit a07c2a27 verified (1 percent of 339,680 = 3,396.80, within 1,500-7,500).

[Seed rationale / automatic clauses] FHA new build by Fairbrook Homes; two access failures (trip charges 09-02, 09-03) moved the due date to 09-11 under the turn-time rule; report completed one day late and delivered within 3 business days; the borrower's factual-error reconsideration (finished area 2,240 -> 2,280 sq ft) changed the value to 354,000 on 09-16; first completion visit on 09-28 found work unfinished; contract closing 10-09 slipped to 10-22 and the lock was extended on 10-09. Checked: no cancellation, no hold, not HPML, report inside validity, the one reconsideration already decided (value_changed 2026-09-16, no fee), delivery on time; the only obligation lit is the late-rush refund, carried by this task. The 2026-09-28 charge (120.00) is what the completion rule gives on that day's record: reinspection fee 200 + FHA 50 - outlay courtesy 30 (standing 1,100) - partner 100, no scheduled closing yet, share 100 percent because no refund stood then.

[Persona] Owen Hadley, friendly first-time buyer; opening: builder finished, appraiser must return, pay for the return visit; phone at opening; SSN last four only when asked; passive acceptance of money coming back to the original card; pays with his debit card when handed the payment; stops when told it is paid.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, SSN4) -> appraisal order -> fee history -> reconsiderations (value_changed decision) -> loan file -> rate lock -> lock pricing entries -> closing -> closing credits -> unlock+call refund (rush entry, 120.00, credit_card) -> unlock_user + borrower pays 90.00 by debit_card.

[Verification run] check_compute's build_env/eval_compute on the world replayed through the real tools (scratch script deleted after closing; re-run with: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0059_residential_mortgage_lender/tasks/appraisal_orders_and_fees --task 1 -> COMPUTE OK): refund 120.0, sensitivities 150.0/82.5/90.0/105.0, baseline 150.0; final inspection charge 90.0, sensitivities 146.25/33.75/52.5/112.5/165.0/120.0, baseline 200.0; skipping the refund -> 120.0. Terminal fee_balance 1220.00 -> 1100.00 -> 1190.00.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules, tool schemas and the nine lookups: refund owed (rush paid after intent to proceed, late), 120.00 to the credit card; then return visit 90.00. Agrees with gold.

[Revision log — audit round 1] O-13 (access deduction double-counted borrower access delays already absorbed by the due date): removed; replaced by extension_cost_points (the lock costs the borrower still bears on the file's lock: extension costs booked to the borrower less every lock-cost waiver on that lock). Closing-slip points now graded on the days of slip from the loan file (no lock read). Lateness shares rescaled to 25/50/100. Refund 105.00 -> 120.00; terminal fee_balance 1205.00 -> 1190.00; standing outlay 1,115.00 -> 1,100.00 (same courtesy tier). O-2: the refund keeps its own counting rule and states that the shared appraisal delay is unchanged (render round: the turn_time overwrite was withdrawn). O-5: the extension read is restricted to the lock on the same loan file and the counting rule names the latest value-changing decision. O-6: the refund is owed on days late of one or more under the counting rule, with cancelled, HPML-flip and pre-intent-to-proceed rush charges left to the base full refund. O-7: the closing-turn part reads the scheduled closing date. O-1: the completion charge excludes reports past validity at the scheduled closing. O-9/O-10: HPML flip exclusion and the scoped 'no stacking' sentence declared (render round: the 'rush on request' overwrite was withdrawn as non-conflicting). O-14: the re-visit method now nets recent reinspection charges (formula change), floored at the trip fee. History depth: a factual-error reconsideration (submitted 2026-09-15, value_changed 2026-09-16) was seeded; it moves the counting endpoint from the delivered date (4 days) to the decision date (5 days), same 50 percent tier, so every figure above holds.

[Revision log — render round 1] Source-only fixes, no scored value moved (refund 120.00, final inspection charge 90.00): turn_time 'appraisal delay' overwrite withdrawn (shared definition kept; the refund states its own count); extension-cost wording now says 'less every lock-cost waiver booked on that lock', as compute does (no waiver on this lock); re-visit rule reads reinspection charges carried on the fee history (charge entries, as compute counts them); completion-clause replacement keeps 'before funding' and names the combined update visit and new-order cases; the rush-at-order overwrite withdrawn; reinspection and no-stacking replacements scoped and sibling-named.

[Revision log — render round 2] Wording only, no scored value moved (refund 120.00, final inspection charge 90.00): the extension-cost points now name their quantity 'the lock costs the borrower still bears' (extension costs booked to the borrower less every lock-cost waiver on that lock), matching compute; tool docstrings say amounts are 'stored rounded to 2 decimal places', matching round() in the bodies.
user_scenario:
You are Owen Hadley, 34, an IT support technician and a first-time buyer, purchasing a newly built house at 2219 Eastwind Court in Gahanna, Ohio, from Fairbrook Homes with a Larkspur FHA loan. You are friendly, a bit chatty and relieved, because the builder finally finished the grading and the back-porch handrails yesterday. You explain that the appraiser came out at the end of September for the final inspection and those items were not done, that your loan officer told you the appraiser has to go back one more time to sign off before your closing on October 22, and that you want to pay for that return visit now so it can be scheduled. That payment is the only thing you are calling to get done; you are not asking for any change to your closing, your rate lock or your closing cost credit.
When the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 6145552194. If the agent needs more to confirm who you are, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 2873; only if pressed for another detail you give your ZIP code, 43230. You do not have any reference numbers handy and tell the agent to look them up. You have no idea what the return visit should cost and you never propose a figure.
If the agent tells you that money is coming back to you on the appraisal, you say that is a nice surprise and that it is fine for it to go back to whatever card it was originally charged to; you do not ask how much or argue about it. When the agent hands the payment for the return visit over to you, you pay it with your debit card, the same way you paid for the first final inspection, and you read the confirmation back. If the agent asks how you want to pay before handing it over, you say your debit card. Once the agent confirms the return visit is paid, you thank them and end the call without bringing up anything else.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: The report type sets the rush, trip and reinspection fees; the dates decide the days late, the counting rule and the borrower's share; the completion flag decides that a completion visit is charged.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the fee history: base fee, rush charge, two trip charges and one reinspection charge dated 2026-09-28, no refund.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the loan file: program, intent-to-proceed date, contract closing date and the closing date currently scheduled.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.appraisal_order_id: b55276e3-0421-4c31-a0fa-de2eeaca7457 — basis: the appraisal order lookup for the verified customer returns one order, the FHA Single-Family report on the Gahanna file; docstring: 'reference number of the appraisal order the rush charge was collected on'. Uniqueness: one order.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.original_fee_entry_id: eebc1eec-6b27-453c-8f26-77b1c148805f — basis: the late-rush refund rule says it 'names the rush charge entry it returns'; the fee history shows exactly one rush_fee charge, entry eebc1eec-6b27-453c-8f26-77b1c148805f, never refunded. Uniqueness: the base, trip and reinspection entries are other lines.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.refund_amount: 120.00 — in scope: delivered order, standard_order, rush charged 2026-08-31 after intent to proceed 2026-07-23. Rush charge standing 150.00 (charged 150.00, refunded 0.00). Counting rule: the order carries one value-changing reconsideration decision (87d5fe64, decided 2026-09-16), so the days late run to that decided date: DAYS(2026-09-11, 2026-09-16) = 5 (the delivered-date tier is not reached). Lateness share: 3-5 days -> 50. Closing-slip points: scheduled closing 2026-10-22 is DAYS(2026-10-09, 2026-10-22) = 13 days after the contract closing -> +20. Extension-cost points: the lock on the file carries extension dce7a1bc with 622.12 booked to the borrower and no waiver -> 622.12 >= 500 -> +10. Share = min(100, max(0, 50 + 20 + 10)) = 80; refund = 150.00 x 80 / 100 = 120.00, kept to the cent.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_method: credit_card — basis: the rule says the refund 'goes back to the card or account that rush charge was collected with'; the rush entry's payment_method is credit_card. Uniqueness: debit_card is the method of the later reinspection charge, not of the rush charge; ach_debit was never used.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_amount: 90.00 — completion pending (subject_to_completion true), report 44 days old at the 2026-10-22 scheduled closing (inside 180 validity days, so this rule and not the update visit charge applies), standard_order. Re-visit rule: a reinspection charge of 120.00 dated 2026-09-28 stands within the last 2 calendar months -> visit base = reinspection fee 200.00 less 120.00 = 80.00, floored at the trip fee 125.00 -> 125.00. Closing-turn part: the scheduled closing date 2026-10-22 is DAYS(2026-10-14, 2026-10-22) = 8 days away -> 6-10 days -> 50 percent of rush fee 150.00 = 75.00. edges.policy_source: The final inspection charge is fixed only after the order's fee history shows the refund owed on any rush charge whose promised delivery date was missed.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The refund write (action 11) books a 120.00 rush_fee refund with reason rush_deadline_missed naming the rush entry; rush_miss_refunds becomes 1 and the borrower's share of the final inspection charge moves from 100 to 75 percent (the standing outlay becomes 1,100.00, still the 30.00 courtesy tier).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the refund must be written before the final inspection charge is evaluated, because the charge reads the refund. edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the refund: no missed-rush refund stands, the borrower's share stays 100 percent and the final inspection charge is 120.00 instead of 90.00; the terminal ledger also lacks the 120.00 refund and fee_balance ends 1340.00 instead of 1190.00.
